summary: The brick, iron and tailored silhouettes establish a convincing Industrial Age, but several pieces miss explicit bible requirements or lose their defining details at stream distance. Restore the fountain, connect the railway camp off-tile, strengthen ownership and resident-role cues, and remove presentation geometry from the assembled street.

elements.fix: Retain the healthy meadow, sparse cinders and isolated sleeper offcuts; keep railway debris subordinate to the countryside.

problems: Repeated rectangular dark patches become an obvious stamped pattern in the assembled scene rather than irregular dampness and wheel wear.
The fine sett pattern becomes visual noise at stream distance; the required longitudinal rectangular structure is weak.
elements.fix: Use larger, clearly rectangular setts oriented along x. Replace the repeated dark rectangles with a few irregular damp patches and restrained longitudinal wheel-polished strips, preserving flush rails, clear gutters and the raised flagstone pavements.
Retain the large empty ochre ring on cream enamel, open gravel centre and sparse brick debris; preserve the ring's contrast at town scale.

problems: The enclosure reads as long horizontal bars rather than cast-iron panels on a distinct raised brick footing.
The central surface reads as a flat terracotta sheet rather than the specified brick surface.
The ownership plate's name, brass border and filled household emblem do not resolve clearly at this camera.
elements.fix: Build a low brick footing with sparse, broad iron panel uprights along the two specified boundaries, keeping the total height around 0.9 m and the frontage open. Add a readable brick surface and enlarge the gate-post enamel plate enough to distinguish 'Ivy', a filled oval, brass border, exposed bolts and the #d9534f ownership strip.

problems: Both crowns rely on similar smooth, flattened foliage blobs, weakening the plane-versus-elm distinction.
Root guards and pavement openings collapse into tiny dark marks rather than readable municipal tree infrastructure.
elements.fix: Within the 30-part pair, give the leaning plane a broken, off-centre crown and the shorter elm a wider, uneven branch spread. Use a few angular foliage masses and clearly outlined low iron guards around visible pavement openings, leaving a usable walking route.

problems: The tall ash reads as a long bare pole with a small rounded tuft.
The ash and elm crowns still look assembled from repeated rounded blobs rather than irregular branching structures.
elements.fix: Redistribute the 36 parts into a visibly forked ash with crown masses at unequal heights, a broad asymmetrical elm and a crooked, sparsely leafed birch. Keep their existing height differences, but replace stacked blobs with larger faceted masses and visible off-axis branches.

problems: The cool, solid-looking lantern does not reveal a readable gas burner or mantle.
The thin shaft loses much of its cast-iron civic character in the assembled view.
elements.fix: Keep the 16-part upright silhouette, but slightly strengthen the post and base. Build a broad square cage with distinguishable glass panels around one compact warm mantle; only that mantle should use glow=true.

problems: The rendered clock tower replaces the explicitly required municipal fountain.
There is no broad basin, upper bowl, visible blue water or four-spout fountain silhouette.
Changing a fountain into a clock also breaks the same-purpose transformation rule.
elements.fix: Replace the clock tower with the specified 52-part cast-iron fountain: approximately 4.5 m stone plinth, broad lower basin, short fluted column, shallow upper bowl and four modest spouts. Keep it around 2.4 m high, with restrained brass fittings and clearly visible non-emissive blue water.
Retain the warm timber slats and broad dark iron end frames, maintaining a two-person width and approximately 0.45 m seat height.
Retain the movable barrow silhouette, large wheels, projecting handle and plain folding canvas cover. Keep the contrasting bread, tins and paper goods grouped into readable masses.

problems: The stop marker reads as a generic yellow circular sign rather than a clearly identifiable enamel tram-wheel emblem.
The timetable case is not legible.
The wheels read as small rim accents beneath the body rather than prominent exposed steam-running gear.
elements.fix: Within 68 parts, retain the short boiler, chimney and timber cabin but enlarge the exposed wheel silhouettes. Give the stop pole a high-contrast enamel wheel-and-spokes emblem and a distinct rectangular timetable case, keeping the canopy narrow and the pavement route clear.

Retain the shallow open lattice girders, timber deck and stone pier noses. Keep both gravel approaches visibly flush with the deck at the bank landings, and preserve the roughly 1 m clearance above water.
Retain the four low brick corner plinths, open construction ground and public-works medallion; keep its filled civic centre visually distinct from the free-lot ring.

problems: The siding visibly terminates within the grassy tile instead of continuing off-tile.
The train therefore reads as a parked display arrangement without a plausible railway connection.
elements.fix: Extend the siding continuously through at least one camp boundary and show an unobstructed off-tile railway approach. Retain the two luxury carriages, striped veranda, compact locomotive, trunks and gathering table within the 88-part budget; keep all wheelsets seated on the rails.

problems: The clerk's lower silhouette does not clearly distinguish a long practical skirt from blocky trousers.
The clerk's brown carried object reads too similarly to the worker's tool case rather than as a ledger.
Pinned hair is not a strong identifying silhouette.
elements.fix: Retain the worker's cap, rolled sleeves, waistcoat and boots. Give the clerk one continuous, slightly flared skirt over visible shoes, a distinct pinned bun and a thin contrasting bound ledger held against the body, retaining both base figures within 48 parts.
Retain the dominant tall top hat, oversized brass civic chain, dark frock coat and rolled charter. Preserve the strong separation from the railway leader's cream coat and bowler.
Retain the cream travel coat, low bowler, waistcoat and concession-map prop. Keep the pocket-watch chain smaller than the Alderman's civic chain and preserve the foreign luggage crest.
Retain the red masonry, pale window surrounds, dark pitched roof and chimney. Keep the entrance and two-storey proportions scaled consistently to the residents.

Retain the enamel tea-room sign, dark timber shopfront, restrained awnings and masonry shell. In town placement, join its customer apron directly to the municipal paving rather than retaining a separate display platform.
Retain the stepped masonry massing, strong cornices, repeated tall windows and restrained copper crown; avoid adding modern curtain glazing or arbitrary machinery.
Retain the chunky hound anatomy and simple brass identification tag. Keep the tag subordinate to the muzzle and body silhouette at resident scale.
Retain the glazed brougham cabin, horse, carriage wheels and restrained brass trim. Keep the paired shafts and harness visually separated from the horse's body when assembling the vehicle.

problems: The residents retain a pale presentation slab in the carriageway, interrupting the continuous sett surface at the tram route.
Repeated street dressing exposes the underlying tile stamp across the road.
The café's separate turf-and-apron platform reads as an asset placed on the square rather than integrated municipal ground.
elements.fix: Strip presentation bases from town instances and place feet directly on the finished ground. Maintain uninterrupted flush rails and setts, vary the road-dressing arrangement between modules, and merge the café frontage into the square's flagstone system with deliberate, traversable edge transitions.
